# PART 41 – DAMAGES

[PART 41 – DAMAGES] Contents of this Part

## Application and definitions

## 41.1

[PART 41 – DAMAGES > 41.1] (1) This Section of this Part applies to proceedings to which SCA s.32A or CCA s.51 applies.

[PART 41 – DAMAGES > 41.1] (2) In this Section –

[PART 41 – DAMAGES > 41.1] (a) ‘SCA s.32A’ means section 32A of the Supreme Court Act 1981 1 ;

[PART 41 – DAMAGES > 41.1] (b) ‘CCA s.51’ means section 51 of the County Courts Act 1984 2 ; and

[PART 41 – DAMAGES > 41.1] (c) ‘award of provisional damages’ means an award of damages for personal injuries under which –

[PART 41 – DAMAGES > 41.1] (i) damages are assessed on the assumption referred to in SCA s.32A or CCA s.51 that the injured person will not develop the disease or suffer the deterioration; and

[PART 41 – DAMAGES > 41.1] (ii) the injured person is entitled to apply for further damages at a future date if he develops the disease or suffers the deterioration.

## Order for an award of provisional damages

## 41.2

[PART 41 – DAMAGES > 41.2] (1) The court may make an order for an award of provisional damages if –

[PART 41 – DAMAGES > 41.2] (a) the particulars of claim include a claim for provisional damages; and

[PART 41 – DAMAGES > 41.2] (b) the court is satisfied that SCA s.32A or CCA s.51 applies.

[PART 41 – DAMAGES > 41.2] (Rule 16.4(1)(d) sets out what must be included in the particulars of claim where the claimant is claiming provisional damages)

[PART 41 – DAMAGES > 41.2] (2) An order for an award of provisional damages –

[PART 41 – DAMAGES > 41.2] (a) must specify the disease or type of deterioration in respect of which an application may be made at a future date;

[PART 41 – DAMAGES > 41.2] (b) must specify the period within which such an application may be made; and

[PART 41 – DAMAGES > 41.2] (c) may be made in respect of more than one disease or type of deterioration and may, in respect of each disease or type of deterioration, specify a different period within which a subsequent application may be made.

[PART 41 – DAMAGES > 41.2] (3) The claimant may make more than one application to extend the period specified under paragraph (2)(b) or (2)(c).

## Application for further damages

## 41.3

[PART 41 – DAMAGES > 41.3] (1) The claimant may not make an application for further damages after the end of the period specified under rule 41.2(2), or such period as extended by the court.

[PART 41 – DAMAGES > 41.3] (2) Only one application for further damages may be made in respect of each disease or type of deterioration specified in the award of provisional damages.

[PART 41 – DAMAGES > 41.3] (3) The claimant must give at least 28 days’ written notice to the defendant of his intention to apply for further damages.

[PART 41 – DAMAGES > 41.3] (4) If the claimant knows –

[PART 41 – DAMAGES > 41.3] (a) that the defendant is insured in respect of the claim; and

[PART 41 – DAMAGES > 41.3] (b) the identity of the defendant’s insurers,

[PART 41 – DAMAGES > 41.3] he must also give at least 28 days’ written notice to the insurers.

[PART 41 – DAMAGES > 41.3] (5) Within 21 days after the end of the 28 day notice period referred to in paragraphs (3) and (4), the claimant must apply for directions.

## IA APPORTIONMENT IN FATALITY CASES

## Apportionment in fatality cases

## 41.3A

[PART 41 – DAMAGES > 41.3A] (1) Where –

[PART 41 – DAMAGES > 41.3A] (a) a claim includes claims arising under –

[PART 41 – DAMAGES > 41.3A] (i) the Fatal Accidents Act 1976; and

[PART 41 – DAMAGES > 41.3A] (ii) the Law Reform (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act 1934; and

[PART 41 – DAMAGES > 41.3A] (b) a single sum of money is ordered or agreed to be paid in satisfaction of the claims,

[PART 41 – DAMAGES > 41.3A] the court will apportion the money between the different claims.

[PART 41 – DAMAGES > 41.3A] (2) Where, in an action in which a claim under the Fatal Accidents Act 1976 is made by or on behalf of more than one person, a single sum of money is ordered or agreed to be paid in satisfaction of the claim, the court will apportion it between the persons entitled to it.

[PART 41 – DAMAGES > 41.3A] (3) Unless it has already been apportioned by the court, a jury or agreement between the parties, the court will apportion money under paragraphs (1) and (2) –

[PART 41 – DAMAGES > 41.3A] (a) when it gives directions under rule 21.11 (control of money received by a child or patient); or

[PART 41 – DAMAGES > 41.3A] (b) if rule 21.11 does not apply, on application by one of the parties in accordance with Part 23.

## II PERIODICAL PAYMENTS UNDER THE DAMAGES ACT 1996

## Scope and interpretation

## 41.4

[PART 41 – DAMAGES > 41.4] (1) This Section of this Part contains rules about the exercise of the court’s powers under section 2(1) of the 1996 Act to order that all or part of an award of damages in respect of personal injury is to take the form of periodical payments.

[PART 41 – DAMAGES > 41.4] (2) In this Section –

[PART 41 – DAMAGES > 41.4] (a) “the 1996 Act” means the Damages Act 1996 3 ;

[PART 41 – DAMAGES > 41.4] (b) “damages” means damages for future pecuniary loss; and

[PART 41 – DAMAGES > 41.4] (c) “periodical payments” means periodical payments under section 2(1) of the 1996 Act 4 .

## Statement of case

## 41.5

[PART 41 – DAMAGES > 41.5] (1) In a claim for damages for personal injury, each party in its statement of case may state whether it considers periodical payments or a lump sum is the more appropriate form for all or part of an award of damages and where such statement is given must provide relevant particulars of the circumstances which are relied on.

[PART 41 – DAMAGES > 41.5] (2) Where a statement under paragraph (1) is not given, the court may order a party to make such a statement.

[PART 41 – DAMAGES > 41.5] (3) Where the court considers that a statement of case contains insufficient particulars under paragraph (1), the court may order a party to provide such further particulars as it considers appropriate.

## Court’s indication to parties

## 41.6

[PART 41 – DAMAGES > 41.6] The court shall consider and indicate to the parties as soon as practicable whether periodical payments or a lump sum is likely to be the more appropriate form for all or part of an award of damages.

## Factors to be taken into account

## 41.7

[PART 41 – DAMAGES > 41.7] When considering –

[PART 41 – DAMAGES > 41.7] (a) its indication as to whether periodical payments or a lump sum is likely to be the more appropriate form for all or part of an award of damages under rule 41.6; or

[PART 41 – DAMAGES > 41.7] (b) whether to make an order under section 2(1)(a) of the 1996 Act,

[PART 41 – DAMAGES > 41.7] the court shall have regard to all the circumstances of the case and in particular the form of award which best meets the claimant’s needs, having regard to the factors set out in Practice Direction 41B.

## The award

## 41.8

[PART 41 – DAMAGES > 41.8] (1) Where the court awards damages in the form of periodical payments, the order must specify –

[PART 41 – DAMAGES > 41.8] (a) the annual amount awarded, how each payment is to be made during the year and at what intervals;

[PART 41 – DAMAGES > 41.8] (b) the amount awarded for future –

[PART 41 – DAMAGES > 41.8] (i) loss of earnings and other income; and

[PART 41 – DAMAGES > 41.8] (ii) care and medical costs and other recurring or capital costs;

[PART 41 – DAMAGES > 41.8] (c) that the claimant’s annual future pecuniary losses, as assessed by the court, are to be paid for the duration of the claimant’s life, or such other period as the court orders; and

[PART 41 – DAMAGES > 41.8] (d) that the amount of the payments shall vary annually by reference to the retail prices index, unless the court orders otherwise under section 2(9) of the 1996 Act.

[PART 41 – DAMAGES > 41.8] (2) Where the court orders that any part of the award shall continue after the claimant’s death, for the benefit of the claimant’s dependants, the order must also specify the relevant amount and duration of the payments and how each payment is to be made during the year and at what intervals.

[PART 41 – DAMAGES > 41.8] (3) Where an amount awarded under paragraph (1)(b) is to increase or decrease on a certain date, the order must also specify –

[PART 41 – DAMAGES > 41.8] (a) the date on which the increase or decrease will take effect; and

[PART 41 – DAMAGES > 41.8] (b) the amount of the increase or decrease at current value.

[PART 41 – DAMAGES > 41.8] (4) Where damages for substantial capital purchases are awarded under paragraph (1)(b)(ii), the order must also specify –

[PART 41 – DAMAGES > 41.8] (a) the amount of the payments at current value;

[PART 41 – DAMAGES > 41.8] (b) when the payments are to be made; and

[PART 41 – DAMAGES > 41.8] (c) that the amount of the payments shall be adjusted by reference to the retail prices index, unless the court orders otherwise under section 2(9) of the 1996 Act.

## Continuity of payment

## 41.9

[PART 41 – DAMAGES > 41.9] (1) An order for periodical payments shall specify that the payments must be funded in accordance with section 2(4) of the 1996 Act, unless the court orders an alternative method of funding.

[PART 41 – DAMAGES > 41.9] (2) Before ordering an alternative method of funding, the court must be satisfied that –

[PART 41 – DAMAGES > 41.9] (a) the continuity of payment under the order is reasonably secure; and

[PART 41 – DAMAGES > 41.9] (b) the criteria set out in Practice Direction 41B are met.

[PART 41 – DAMAGES > 41.9] (3) An order under paragraph (2) must specify the alternative method of funding.

## Assignment or charge

## 41.10

[PART 41 – DAMAGES > 41.10] Where the court under section 2(6)(a) of the 1996 Act is satisfied that special circumstances make an assignment or charge of periodical payments necessary, it shall, in deciding whether or not to approve the assignment or charge, also have regard to the factors set out in Practice Direction 41B.

## Footnotes

[PART 41 – DAMAGES > Footnotes] 1. 1981 c.54. Section 32A was inserted by section 6(1) of the Administration of Justice Act 1982 (c.53). Back to text
